general_information.Syllabus Name: Đề án dịch vụ quản trị du lịch và lữ hành/Hospitality Planning and development
general_information.Description: After taking the “basic courses” to get an overview of event organization, students will get the deeper knowledge in planning and running a Tourism and Hospitality Event such as a Thematic Tour, an artistic show, an exhibition, a specific performance, etc. Students see themselves as event operators and they are being required to keep their mind on all relevant elements of an event. Thus, they need expertise and skills in a diverse range of disciplines and nationally, there is a shortage of relevant skills. This course offers opportunities for students to gain valuable skills that make them highly employable in the Touristic Event organization market, and allows them to contribute to a much needed and fast changing professional area. Students work in groups to brainstorm business ideas, then develop a business plan, implement this plan within a semester period. The results of this project will be presented in front of an examiner panel.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend more than 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.
general_information.Note: Progress marks: - Participation: 10% - 03 Progress test: 90% Conditions to pass: Each progress mark: > 0 Grade Average >= 5/10

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: To identify the key characteristics of events, events industry bodies, in order to understand the business of events management as a service activity
To understand the scope and scale of the events business and the determinants of demand for events
To identify the social, economic, political impact and developmental implications of running events
To understand the planning process for events, including the budgetary organization of events, marketing, catering and technical provisions.
To identify issues of risk management in terms of event planning, operations and the issues involved in closing down an event
To intergrate a theoratical framework in to an event project

assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed. - 10 to 30 minutes

assessments.Question Type: 10-15 students per group. Groups and groups ideas are determined on the second session of the course. Work will be break down into stages and examined during the course. The event will be deployed at the end of the semestre.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on topics of studied units
assessments.Grading Guide: Group presentation in class room and outdoor event.
assessments.Note: All assignments should be typed and double-spaced with 11-point font, and must be submitted in both soft and hard copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission Evaluation will be based on both written report and implementation (reccomemded 30%, 70% accordingly) - Minimum length of the group assignment should be 10 pages, excluding appendices

assessments.Question Type: Each student shoud make at least 1 individual presentation, case analysis during the course in front of the class. Topics will be varied based on the topics in the textbook.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on the given exercise or case study at the beginning of the course.

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice, exercises or essay questions
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Quizzes will test for knowledge of subjects in the chapter assigned for that day.
assessments.Note: These quizzes will be given at various times during class (beginning, middle or end). Total number of quizzes: 3
